turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Morning, Mr. Petrescu. How's the harvest going?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Slow soybeans are in, corn still standing. Too wet last week.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Well, I hope it dries out for you. Can you tell me your full name and date of birth? Just to confirm. Bogdan Petrescu,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: March 11th, 1952.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: And the front desk said you moved. Yep, we sold the old place. New address is 8817 County Road 12, Seward, Nebraska.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Phone's the same,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it. I'll make sure that's updated. So what's bothering you today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: These rough spots on top of my head. My wife Alina says they look like sandpaper. They catch on the comb and bleed a little when I scratch them. Been a few months.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do any of them hurt?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, they don't hurt. Any spot that's growing fast or bleeding on its own. No, nothing like that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Do you wear a hat out in the field?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: A seed cap, the kind with the mesh in the back. Sunscreen, no, I never bother with it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, any changes in your medicines?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Same as always. Adorvastatin 20 milligrams at night and a baby aspirin, the 81 every morning. No allergies.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good. Oh. And how's the spot on your left cheek, where we took off the basal cell back, in 2021?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Fine, I don't even think about it. My neighbor Roy just had a melanoma taken off his ear though,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: scared him half to death. I bet. Let's have a look. Your scalp has a lot of background sun damage. I count six rough, gritty, pink scaly spots. three to eight millimeters on the top and front of the scalp. None of them are thick, tender, or growing like a bump, so nothing that worries me for a skin cancer today. The scar on your left cheek is well -heeled, and I don't see anything coming back there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's good.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you lift your shirt so I can check your back? Okay, you have several brown, waxy, stuck -on spots on your back, about one centimeter each. Those are seborrheic keratosis. They're harmless, no treatment needed.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My barnacles, Elina calls them.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's exactly what they look like. So the spots on your scalp are actinic keratosis. They're precancers from years of sun. Most never turn into cancer, but But some can become a squamous cell skin cancer, so I'd like to freeze all six today with liquid nitrogen. Okay.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: All right, it'll sting for a bit. First one. Second. Third.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Fourth.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Fifth. And sixth. That's all six done.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, that wasn't bad.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Over the next few days, they'll get red. Maybe blister, then crust, and peel off in one to three weeks. You can put a little petroleum jelly on them. If any spot hasn't healed in six weeks or starts growing, come back and we'll biopsy it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Now the big one, the sun.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every morning,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: a broad -spectrum sunscreen, SPF 30 or higher, on your scalp, face, ears, and the backs of your hands, reapply every two hours when you're out in the field and trade the seed cap for a wide -brimmed hat that covers your ears and neck. Long sleeves help too.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Alina's going to love that. She's been on me about a hat for years.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: She's right. If a lot more of these come back, there's a cream called flurrorassel we can use to treat the whole scalp at once. But let's see how you do. I'd like to see you in six months for a full skin check, since you've had a skin cancer before.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Six months, I'll put it on the calendar after harvest.
